historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-Inca Cañari indigenous settlement of Guapondelig
historical_names.name: Guapondelig

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded 12 April 1557 by Gil Ramírez Dávalos under orders of Viceroy Andrés Hurtado de Mendoza

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Guane indigenous settlement and toponym prior to Spanish colonial reduction

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Chimila (Ette Ennaka) indigenous territory of Cacique Upar / Eupari prior to Spanish foundation

historical_names.name: Ciudad de los Santos Reyes del Valle de Upar

historical_names.date_source_note: Valledupar Act of Independence proclaimed on 4 February 1813; republican contraction to Valledupar

historical_names.date_source_note: Renamed Bello by decree of the Sovereign State of Antioquia on 28 December 1883 in honour of Andrés Bello

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 31 May 1565 by Diego de Villarroel at Ibatín as San Miguel de Tucumán y Nueva Tierra de Promisión

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated to its present site at La Toma on 29 September 1685 under Governor Fernando de Mendoza Mate de Luna as San Miguel de Tucumán

historical_names.date_source_note: Designated seat of the Intendencia de Salta del Tucumán under the Royal Ordinance of Intendants of 28 January 1782 using the shortened official name Salta
historical_names.name: Salta

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 29 July 1525 by Rodrigo de Bastidas on the Bay of Santa Marta in Tairona territory; retained the name continuously
historical_names.name: Santa Marta

settlements.name: Ibagué

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 14 October 1550 by Andrés López de Galarza as Villa de San Bonifacio de Ibagué del Valle de las Lanzas; relocated to its current site on 7 February 1551
historical_names.name: San Bonifacio de Ibagué

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened to Ibagué in republican administrative usage upon the establishment of Gran Colombia

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1532 at the Tallán settlement of Tangarará as the first Spanish city in Peru

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated to the Piura valley in 1534 (and permanently to its present site on the Piura River in 1588) as San Miguel de Piura

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 7 December 1760 by Aragonese Capuchin missionary Fray Lucas de Zaragoza on the Guarapiche River at the post-1718 Sitio de Maturín (following an earlier 1722 attempt)

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded by Breidenbach brothers upon land deed registration

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially established as the ecclesiastical parish of San José de Maracay on 5 March 1701 by Bishop Diego de Baños y Sotomayor

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened to Maracay in republican administrative usage following Venezuelan independence
historical_names.name: Maracay

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 13 June 1562 by Juan Jufré in the Huarpe Tulum Valley as San Juan de la Frontera; relocated slightly south in 1593 by Luis Jufré

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened to San Juan in republican administrative usage following the May Revolution in the Río de la Plata
historical_names.name: San Juan

historical_names.date_source_note: First permanent settlement at the Bolivian coastal cove of La Chimba established by prospector Juan López in November 1866; town decree signed 22 October 1868

historical_names.date_source_note: Declared Puerto Mayor of Antofagasta by Bolivia on 8 May 1871, formalising the name Antofagasta; under Chilean administration since 14 February 1879

historical_names.date_source_note: Originated in the early 18th century (c. 1736) as the lakeshore estate and settlement of La Punta de Don Francisco on Lake Maracaibo south of Maracaibo

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 17 February 1621 by Captain Pedro Gutiérrez de Lugo and Father Gabriel de Mendoza as a pueblo de doctrina on Mariche indigenous territory

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened to Petare in republican administrative usage following Venezuelan independence; elevated to Cantón de Petare in 1822
historical_names.name: Petare

historical_names.date_source_note: Jesuit mission reduction established circa 1757 by Father José Bahamonde near the Nanay–Amazon confluence among Napeano and Iquito peoples

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as a Peruvian Amazonian river port and naval station under the name Iquitos on 5 January 1864; became capital of Loreto in 1897
historical_names.name: Iquitos

known_aliases: san juan de vera de las siete corrientes
San Juan de Vera de las Siete Corrientes
settlements.name: Corrientes

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 3 April 1588 by Adelantado Juan Torres de Vera y Aragón as San Juan de Vera de las Siete Corrientes
historical_names.name: San Juan de Vera de las Siete Corrientes

historical_names.date_source_note: Capital of the newly created Province of Corrientes by decree of Supreme Director Gervasio Antonio de Posadas on 10 September 1814 using the shortened official name Corrientes
historical_names.name: Corrientes

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Timoto-Cuica indigenous settlement of Tatuy on the Chama River terrace; municipal capital of Municipio Libertador, Mérida State.

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 9 October 1558 by Juan Rodríguez Suárez as Mérida (relocated to Tatuy in 1559–1560).

historical_names.date_source_note: Relocated to the Chama terrace and styled Santiago de los Caballeros de Mérida during the colonial era.

historical_names.date_source_note: Venezuelan Independence (5 July 1811); modern republican name Mérida.
historical_names.name: Mérida

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as civil parish in Guárico Llanos
historical_names.name: San Nicolás de Bari de El Rastro

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened name in Venezuelan national census records

historical_names.date_source_note: Established as Distrito Girardot in Aragua State in 1881 (centred on Maracay, succeeding the 1879–1880 Territorio Federal Maracay / Distrito Maracay); reconstituted as the autonomous Municipio Girardot on 15 June 1989 under Venezuela's Organic Law of Municipal Regime
historical_names.name: Girardot

historical_names.date_source_note: Definitively founded on its present site on 24 May 1612 by Diego de Ospina y Medinilla as Nuestra Señora de la Limpia Concepción del Valle de Neiva, following earlier short-lived foundations in 1539 and 1550

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially styled Neiva as provincial capital within Gran Colombia (17 December 1819) and modern Colombia

historical_names.date_source_note: Fishing cove documented upon creation of Santa Province
historical_names.name: Chimbote

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected as the ecclesiastical parish of Nuestra Señora del Pilar on 22 March 1772 by Bishop Manuel Antonio de la Torre around the earlier 1729 chapel on the Luján River (with the civil Partido del Pilar formally recognised by the Cabildo of Luján on 5 March 1774)
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora del Pilar

historical_names.date_source_note: Site of the Treaty of Pilar on 23 February 1820, using the shortened official name Pilar in republican administration
historical_names.name: Pilar

historical_names.date_source_note: Jesuit reduction of San Fernando del Río Negro founded on 26 August 1750 among Abipón people; site remained known as San Fernando through the 18th and 19th centuries
historical_names.name: San Fernando del Río Negro

historical_names.date_source_note: Formally established on 2 February 1878 as Colonia Resistencia upon the arrival of the first Friulian settlers, becoming capital of Chaco
historical_names.name: Resistencia

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Cumanagoto indigenous settlement at the mouth of the Cumaná (Manzanares) River, attested upon early Spanish contact (1498–1515) and site of the 27 November 1515 Franciscan mission

historical_names.date_source_note: Short-lived Spanish settlement founded by Gonzalo de Ocampo in 1521 on the site of Cumaná

historical_names.date_source_note: Pre-colonial Panzaleo settlement and Inca tambo (Hampatu / Hambato) on the Qhapaq Ñan documented by early Spanish chroniclers

historical_names.date_source_note: Erected in 1773 as the colonial parish of Llanogrande (Nuestra Señora del Palmar de Llanogrande) in the jurisdiction of Buga
historical_names.name: Llanogrande

historical_names.date_source_note: Officially established as the municipality and cantón of Palmira by Gran Colombia's Law of Territorial Division on 25 June 1824
historical_names.name: Palmira

historical_names.date_source_note: Founded on 27 November 1620 by Governor Francisco de la Hoz Berrío and Bishop Gonzalo de Angulo as the pueblo de doctrina of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Turmero
historical_names.name: Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de Turmero

historical_names.date_source_note: Shortened to Turmero in republican administrative usage following Venezuelan independence
historical_names.name: Turmero
